MARKET COMMENTARY3

blocks.html: Within the asset-based finance (ABF) market, the first quarter of 2026 was characterized by heightened market volatility, persistent geopolitical uncertainty, and shifting expectations around the pace of monetary easing. Despite wider credit spreads and fluctuations in government bond yields, institutional demand for private, asset-backed income strategies remained robust. In our view, investors continued to favor ABF for its combination of contractual cash flows, structural downside protection, and reduced dependence on corporate earnings or refinancing conditions.

blocks.html: ABF origination activity remained healthy during the quarter, supported by ongoing bank retrenchment, growing financing needs across consumers, small businesses, and hard assets, and increasing adoption of non-bank lending solutions. Consistent with broader industry trends, capital formation continued to migrate toward asset-backed structures, with both borrowers and investors seeking more customized financing solutions backed by identifiable collateral and predictable cash flows. During this time, we remained disciplined, emphasizing conservative leverage levels, meaningful first-loss protection, dynamic borrowing bases, performance covenants, and strong servicing and reporting frameworks. These structural protections continue to distinguish our approach to ABF from many areas of traditional corporate credit, where covenant packages remain comparatively less robust.

blocks.html: Yields across many areas of private ABF continued to compare favorably with traditional fixed income and increasingly competitive direct lending markets. In our view, some of the most compelling relative value opportunities remain concentrated in receivables finance, specialty consumer and small business lending, equipment and hard assets, and other self-amortizing cash-flow-generating collateral pools. These sectors continue to benefit from structural market inefficiencies, limited bank participation, and the ability to negotiate bespoke transaction terms directly with originators.

blocks.html: Collateral performance across most ABF verticals remained generally stable during the quarter. Consumer credit metrics continued to normalize from post-pandemic levels, with pressure concentrated primarily among lower-credit-quality borrowers, unsecured consumer lending, and select subprime segments. However, these trends were largely anticipated by lenders and reflected in existing structures through lower advance rates, enhanced credit enhancement, excess spread, and tighter collateral eligibility criteria. Meanwhile, performance across many commercial, receivables-based, and hard-asset sectors remained resilient, supported by healthy collateral coverage and strong cash-flow generation. We continue to see a meaningful divergence between higher-quality and lower-quality credit exposures, reinforcing the importance of asset selection and underwriting discipline.

blocks.html: Looking forward, we believe the environment remains favorable for experienced ABF investors. Growing focus on the asset class from allocators, continued expansion of non-bank lending, and an increasingly broad opportunity set continue to support long-term market growth. At the same time, heightened dispersion across asset types, originators, and underlying borrower cohorts reinforces the importance of manager selection, rigorous underwriting, and active portfolio monitoring. In our view, ABF remains well positioned as a diversified and defensive segment of private credit, offering attractive risk-adjusted return potential through a combination of current income, structural protection, and exposure to essential components of the real economy.

blocks.html: We deployed capital across a diversified set of technology-enabled asset-based finance opportunities, with a consistent emphasis on seniority, structural protection, and multiple paths to repayment. Investments included a senior secured first-lien growth facility to an enterprise software provider serving the cybersecurity and endpoint management market, a forward-flow partnership purchasing diversified customer acquisition receivables originated by a leading alternative asset manager, and a combined first- lien debt and structured equity investment in a workplace savings technology platform undertaking a transformative acquisition. The portfolio continues to emphasize conservative attachment points, durable cash flow generation, and structures that provide both principal protection and attractive risk-adjusted return potential.

blocks.html: Credit Risk. The Fund is subject to significant credit risk (i.e., the risk that an issuer or borrower will default in the payment of principal and/or interest on an instrument) in light of its investment strategy. Credit risk also includes the risk that a counterparty will be unwilling or unable to meet its obligations. Financial strength and solvency of an issuer or borrower are the primary factors influencing credit risk. In addition, degree of subordination, lack or inadequacy of collateral or credit enhancement for a debt instrument may affect its credit risk.

When the Fund makes a senior secured loan to a portfolio company, it will generally take a security interest in the available assets of the portfolio company, including the equity interests of its subsidiaries, which should help mitigate the risk that the Fund will not be repaid. However, there is a risk that the collateral securing the Fund’s loans may decrease in value over time, may be difficult to sell in a timely manner, may be difficult to appraise, and may fluctuate in value based upon the success of the business and market conditions, including as a result of the inability of the portfolio company to raise additional capital.

In addition, the Fund may borrow funds for the purpose of making distributions to Investors, generally in anticipation of amounts to be received by the Fund from Fund Investments. blocks.html: Epidemics, Pandemics, Outbreaks of Disease and Public Health Issues. Neuberger’s business activities as well as the activities of the Fund and its operations and investments could be materially adversely affected by outbreaks of disease, epidemics and public health issues in Asia, Europe, North America, the Middle East and/or globally, such as COVID-19 (and other novel coronaviruses), Ebola, H1N1 flu, H7N9 flu, H5N1 flu, Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome, or SARS, or other epidemics, pandemics, outbreaks of disease or public health issues. In particular, coronavirus, or COVID-19, has spread rapidly around the world since its initial emergence in December 2019 and has negatively affected (and may continue to negatively affect or materially impact) the global economy, global equity markets and supply chains (including as a result of quarantines and other government-directed or mandated measures or actions to stop the spread of outbreaks). Although the long-term effects of coronavirus, or COVID-19 (and the actions and measures taken by governments around the world to halt the spread of such virus), cannot currently be predicted, previous occurrences of other epidemics, pandemics and outbreaks of disease, such as H5N1, H1N1 and the Spanish flu, had material adverse effects on the economies, equity markets and operations of those countries and jurisdictions in which they were most prevalent. A recurrence of an outbreak of any kind of epidemic, communicable disease, virus or major public health issue could cause a slowdown in the levels of economic activity generally (or push the world or local economies into recession), which would be reasonably likely to adversely affect the business, financial condition and operations of Neuberger and the Fund. Neuberger’s business activities as well as the activities of the Fund and its operations and investments could be materially adversely affected by outbreaks of disease, epidemics and public health issues in Asia, Europe, North America, the Middle East and/or globally, such as COVID-19 (and other novel coronaviruses), Ebola, H1N1 flu, H7N9 flu, H5N1 flu, Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome, or SARS, or other epidemics, pandemics, outbreaks of disease or public health issues. In particular, coronavirus, or COVID-19, has spread rapidly around the world since its initial emergence in December 2019 and has negatively affected (and may continue to negatively affect or materially impact) the global economy, global equity markets and supply chains (including as a result of quarantines and other government-directed or mandated measures or actions to stop the spread of outbreaks). Although the long-term effects of coronavirus, or COVID-19 (and the actions and measures taken by governments around the world to halt the spread of such virus), cannot currently be predicted, previous occurrences of other epidemics, pandemics and outbreaks of disease, such as H5N1, H1N1 and the Spanish flu, had material adverse effects on the economies, equity markets and operations of those countries and jurisdictions in which they were most prevalent. A recurrence of an outbreak of any kind of epidemic, communicable disease, virus or major public health issue could cause a slowdown in the levels of economic activity generally (or push the world or local economies into recession), which would be reasonably likely to adversely affect the business, financial condition and operations of Neuberger and the Fund. Should these or other major public health issues, including pandemics, arise or spread farther (or continue to worsen), Neuberger and the Fund could be adversely affected by more stringent travel restrictions (such as mandatory quarantines and social distancing), additional limitations on Neuberger’s (or the Fund’s) operations and business activities and governmental actions limiting the movement of people and goods between regions and other activities or operations.
